blocks.value: Congratulations! You now know enough to understand a basic stock chart. Before learning technical indicators, let's combine everything you've learned so far.
Imagine This: Learning the stock market is like learning to read. First you learned letters, then words, then sentences. Charts are the first complete paragraph you can now understand.
When looking at a chart, start by identifying the timeframe, observe whether the overall trend is moving up or down, notice the trading volume, and then study the candlesticks.
If you see higher prices over several weeks, increasing volume and mostly bullish candles, buyers have generally been stronger during that period.
Don't try to predict tomorrow's price yet. First become comfortable reading what has already happened.
You have completed the first 50 lessons! You now understand money, businesses, companies, the stock market, buying shares, price movement and reading charts.
